newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu back in Israel after Washington summit.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu back in Israel after Washington summit.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Banjamin Netanyahu landed in Israel on Thursday after a two-day Washington peace summit that Palestinians said was a failure.

Right-wing activists lined the Tel Aviv-Jerusalem highway to cheer Netanyahu for not making concessions to Palestinian President Yasser Arafat in talks on a promised Israeli troop redeployment in the West Bank town of Hebron.
Netanyahu appealed to Palestinians to remain calm and have faith in negotiations scheduled to resume on Sunday at Erez checkpoint on the border between Israel and self-ruled Gaza.

"I want to say something to Palestinian viewers. There are no winners and no losers if we fight each other," Netanyahu said. "If we fight each other and if we return to bloody riots, we will both be losers. If we walk together on the process of peace...we will both be winners," Netanyahu said.
Netanyahu returned on Thursday from a White House crisis summit, hailed as a success by Israel, called after a week of violence.

Palestinians called the summit a failure after Palestinian President Yasser Arafat failed to win a target date for a long-delayed Israeli troop redeployment in the West Bank town of Hebron or an Israeli pledge to close a Jerusalem tunnel whose opening last week sparked bloody clashes which killed more than 70.
